changes.change: Added full Signal Preservation and Non-Subordination requirements: (1) section 3A states the purpose (the prioritisation layer sits above the existing signal estate and is not a second activation authority) and seven required invariants (existing signals/supporting signals continue firing unchanged; thresholds/activation keys/package lineage/runtime eligibility unchanged; tier/role/consolidation never gate activation; independent signals only become supporting-only under an explicit approved relationship rule; constituent signals remain identifiable and provenance-complete after consolidation; no Knowledge Bus promotion status changes; the 109 scenarios validate behaviour but never authorise signal suppression/retirement/threshold change; SIGNALS_INTENTIONALLY_RETIRED must be 0 absent cited prior authority); (2) section 3A.3 states the revised five-layer authority hierarchy (signal activation estate defines what fires -> domain clinical authority defines meaning -> cross-domain authority defines consolidation/prioritisation -> product authority defines presentation -> acceptance scenarios validate only); (3) section 4.4 requires the Phase 0 signal activation baseline inventory (signal ID, activation key, package/source, promotion/runtime status, primary biomarker, supporting biomarkers/signals, derived-marker dependencies, DTO/frontend exposure, regression evidence) and ties it into Checkpoint 0; (4) section 7.3 adds an explicit non-subordination line to the concern-construction service requirements; (5) section 12 adds STOP conditions 16-21 covering signal disabling, provenance loss, activation-behaviour change, promotion/eligibility change, silent retirement by a newer document, and unresolvable contract-vs-signal-estate conflict, each required to be reported as a provenance conflict and escalated rather than silently resolved in favour of the newest document; (6) sections 13 and 15 add the five mandatory closure metrics (SIGNAL_ACTIVATION_BASELINE_TOTAL, SIGNAL_ACTIVATION_PRESERVED_TOTAL, SUPPORTING_SIGNAL_BASELINE_TOTAL, SUPPORTING_SIGNAL_PRESERVED_TOTAL, SIGNALS_INTENTIONALLY_RETIRED) to both the required-evidence list and the START completion response.

changes.change: Added an explicit 'Compilation scope boundary' paragraph: compile only the rules necessary to reproduce the 109 approved scenarios and their governing structural context; any domain-ruleset band/threshold recorded as unset (e.g. marked '[U]') must be excluded from compilation and recorded as a follow-on item, never estimated.
changes.reason: User-identified gap during post-hardening review: STOP condition 1 (section 12) is scoped to 'any of the 109 scenarios' and would not obviously fire for a domain-ruleset table row with an unset threshold that no approved scenario exercises (concrete example found: haematology ruleset HAEM-U-D-5, 'marked leucocytosis with abnormal differential pattern', recorded as '[U] -- threshold not set' inside an otherwise-governed within-days urgency table). The prior general prohibition ('do not invent a new clinical rule') and the fail-closed compiler requirement already existed but did not explicitly name this failure mode. A proactive scope-bounding instruction was chosen over a 16th STOP condition because: (1) it prevents the ambiguity rather than reacting to it; (2) an unset '[U]' threshold is an already-known, already-classified authoring gap, not a novel discovery requiring escalation, so a STOP is the wrong severity; (3) this pattern recurs across multiple domains (e.g. iron/inflammatory IRIN-U2/IRIN-U3, thyroid THY-U2), so a STOP condition would trigger repeatedly for a uniformly-already-decided disposition rather than being handled once by a scoping rule.
changes.classification: Scope-narrowing safety correction. Reduces risk (closes an ambiguity that could permit undetected clinical-rule invention); does not expand scope, does not touch clinical content, does not change front matter, does not require re-running Stage 2A/2B verification against new authority files.
